title: Supreme Court Rejects Trump Bid to Revive University Research Cuts
summary: The justices left in place a lower-court decision to block the administration from cutting millions in grants to University of California researchers over perceived ties to diversity initiatives.

The Supreme Court on Monday rejected a request from the Trump administration seeking to revive cuts to tens of millions of dollars in research grants to the University of California.


The court’s rejection of the case leaves in place a lower-court ruling that found the Trump administration had most likely violated the First Amendment when it terminated the grants over perceived connections to diversity initiatives.


The announcement by the justices came on a routine orders list and gave no reasoning, as is typical. No dissents were noted.


The decision was a blow to President Trump’s pressure campaign against one of the country’s largest and most prestigious public university systems. The[University of California](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/02/24/us/justice-department-ucla-lawsuit.html) has been[a major focus](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/09/17/us/university-of-california-berkeley-regents-meeting.html) of the president’s critiques of the country’s universities for much of his second term. The 10-campus system has about 560,000 students and employees and receives about $17 billion in federal funding each year.


Matthew J. Tragesser, a Justice Department spokesman, said in a statement that the administration would continue its court fight to cancel the federal research grants and advocate “the executive branch’s lawful authority to administer federal funding programs.”


Erwin Chemerinsky, the dean of the law school at the University of California, Berkeley, who argued on behalf of the researchers, said he was “obviously delighted” that the justices had declined to hear the case and that courts had upheld that “the government cannot cut off grants based on the perceived viewpoint of the research.”
